summary:
I developed Astra_The Raza , an interactive space mission simulation game that takes players through the complete lifecycle of a space mission, from early concept planning to active orbital operations.
My game directly addresses the challenge by turning complex aerospace engineering into hands-on gameplay. Players define mission objectives, configure spacecraft hardware, select scientific payloads, and choose launch vehicles and target orbits. Using real-world space datasets, the simulator challenges individuals or teams to balance strict engineering constraints—including budget, mass, power, data rates, communications, and mission lifetime—while providing post-mission scoring and trade-off analysis.
This project is important because real spaceflight requires careful systems engineering and collaborative decision-making. By making mission design accessible and engaging, Astra  demystifies how aerospace teams solve high-stakes trade-offs and inspires the next generation of space explorers and engineers.

Project Overview: Space Mission Design Game

What does it do and how does it work?
Our Space Mission Design Game is an interactive simulation that puts players in the role of an aerospace engineer and mission director. Players design custom spacecraft, manage fuel and budget constraints, calculate launch trajectories, and navigate real-world orbital mechanics to complete objectives like satellite deployment, lunar landings, or deep-space exploration. The game uses a physics-based simulation engine to test player designs in real time, providing immediate visual feedback on structural stability, thrust-to-weight ratios, and orbital paths.

What benefits does it have?

  • Hands-on STEM Learning: It turns complex aerospace and physics concepts—such as gravity assists, delta-v, and atmospheric drag—into intuitive, trial-and-error gameplay.
  • Problem-Solving & Critical Thinking: Players must balance competing constraints like weight, fuel capacity, and cost, encouraging iterative design and analytical thinking.
  • Accessible Engagement: It removes the barrier of expensive lab equipment or complex CAD software, allowing anyone to experience the fundamentals of rocket science from a standard computer.

What is the intended impact of the project?
The primary goal of this project is to inspire curiosity in space exploration and aerospace engineering among students and casual gamers alike. By bridging the gap between entertainment and education, we aim to demystify rocket science, build confidence in STEM subjects, and encourage players to view engineering failures as valuable data points on the path to success.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
(I use github, VS code editor ,claud and gemini to complete this project and use claud and website loveable to create my website and live it . )

  • Game Engine & Software: Unity (or Unreal Engine / Godot) for 3D rendering, physics simulation, and scene management.
  • Coding Languages: C# (or Python / C++) for scripting orbital mechanics, UI logic, and spacecraft modular assembly.
  • Design & Audio Tools: Blender for 3D spacecraft and planetary modeling, Figma for UI/UX wireframing, and Audacity for sound effects.
  • Collaboration & Version Control: Git and GitHub for source code management and team collaboration.
  • Hardware: Standard development PCs/laptops for coding, 3D rendering, and playtesting across different screen resolutions.

How is your project creative?

  • Modular Sandbox Freedom: Rather than forcing a single "correct" rocket design, the game allows players to creatively combine boosters, fuel tanks, payloads, and sensors in endless configurations.
  • Interactive Visualization: Complex mathematical data (like apoapsis, periapsis, and fuel burn rates) is translated into clean, color-coded visual trajectory lines and dynamic HUD elements.
  • Dynamic Mission Scenarios: Players face unexpected space hazards—such as solar flares, micrometeoroids, or communication blackouts—requiring creative on-the-fly mission adjustments.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Realism vs. Playability: We carefully balanced accurate Newtonian physics with approachable game mechanics so the game feels authentic without becoming overwhelmingly difficult for beginners.
  • User Interface (UI) Clarity: Because space flight involves many variables, we prioritized a clean, clutter-free interface with progressive tutorials so new players aren't intimidated.
  • Performance Optimization: We optimized physics calculations and 3D assets to ensure smooth frame rates even when rendering complex multi-stage rockets and planetary orbits.
  • Accessibility & Replayability: We included multiple difficulty modes, sandbox freedom, and tiered mission challenges to appeal to both casual players and hardcore space enthusiasts.
